_schema: Hand-maintained data for the meta-omics SIG conveyor-belt site. Strict JSON: no comments, no trailing commas. Three vocabularies are kept apart and must not be blended. (1) repoStatus = a string copied VERBATIM from the 'Samplesheet Chaining - Validation Table' in PLAN.md; edges not in that table have no repoStatus key at all. (2) Site annotations (caveat, siteState, routable, layer, routingBasis) are this site's own notes and are always rendered as such, never as a status. (3) statusClass is a render class only. Two version fields exist and must not be conflated: stations[].release is the version whose documentation the `requires` list was read from (see requiresReadFrom), while datasets[].siteState[id].version is the version actually used for that dataset. The site shows the executed version, and both when they differ. When you change PLAN.md's validation table, change this file.

stations.label: fetchngs
stations.blurb: Fetches public sequencing data from SRA/ENA accessions and emits the FASTQ files plus a generic samplesheet describing them.
requires: ids.csv - one accession per line (not a CSV samplesheet)

stations.label: detaxizer
stations.blurb: Screens reads for contaminant or host sequence and can filter them out. Defaults to human contamination screening (tax2filter = Homo sapiens), but the target taxon and reference are configurable. It can also emit samplesheets for downstream pipelines - one of two pipelines in this chain that do, the other being proteinfamilies.
requires: --input samplesheet: sample, short_reads_fastq_1, short_reads_fastq_2, long_reads_fastq_1 - gzipped FASTQ only
--kraken2db - defaults to downloading k2_standard (~60 GB) from S3; point at a local copy. Only fetched when kraken2 classification actually runs
--classification_bbduk with --fasta_bbduk takes an arbitrary contaminant FASTA instead, so a small target (phiX, 5.4 kb) needs no kraken2 database at all
--skip_filter for detect-only mode - but it also disables the downstream samplesheet emitter, which is fed a channel that stays empty unless the filter ran
--generate_downstream_samplesheets with --generate_pipeline_samplesheets (taxprofiler and/or mag only)

stations.label: reference genomes
stations.blurb: Not an nf-core pipeline. Reference sequences with taxonomy IDs, sourced separately (for example via NCBI datasets). Drawn because createtaxdb has to be fed from somewhere, and it is not fed by the read stream.

stations.label: createtaxdb
stations.blurb: Builds custom taxonomic classification databases from reference sequences for downstream profilers.
requires: --input samplesheet: id, taxid, and at least one of fasta_dna / fasta_aa
--dbname
at least one --build_<tool> flag (no tool is built by default)

stations.label: ampliseq
stations.blurb: Processes 16S/ITS/COI amplicon reads into ASVs, taxonomy tables and diversity metrics.
requires: --input samplesheet: sample, fastq_1 (fastq_2 required for paired-end)
--FW_primer and --RV_primer (skippable only with --skip_cutadapt)
--metadata (optional, recommended for downstream analysis)

stations.label: taxprofiler
stations.blurb: Taxonomic profiling of shotgun reads across multiple classifiers at once.
requires: --input samplesheet: sample, run_accession, instrument_platform, fastq_1, fastq_2, fasta
--databases sheet: tool, db_name, db_params, db_path (db_type optional)
one --run_<tool> flag per profiler, matching a database row

stations.label: mag
stations.blurb: Assembles shotgun reads into contigs and bins them into MAGs - draft genomes inferred from metagenomic sequencing.
requires: --input samplesheet header: sample, group, short_reads_1, short_reads_2, long_reads
short_reads_platform - required whenever short reads are given
long_reads_platform - required whenever long reads are given
run (optional) - run/lane-wise concatenation before assembly

stations.label: magmap
stations.blurb: Maps reads against a set of MAGs or genomes to produce coverage and abundance profiles.
requires: --input samplesheet: sample, fastq_1, fastq_2 (fastq_2 omitted for single-end)
--genomeinfo: accno, genome_fna (genome_gff optional; Prokka annotates genomes without it)

stations.label: funcscan
stations.blurb: Screens assembled contigs for antimicrobial peptides, AMR genes and biosynthetic gene clusters.

stations.label: phageannotator
stations.blurb: Identifies and annotates phage sequences in assembled contigs.
stations.devNote: No tagged release - development branch only. Unsuitable for a pinned benchmark run as things stand.

stations.label: phyloplace
stations.blurb: Places query sequences onto a reference phylogenetic tree.

stations.label: metapep
stations.blurb: Predicts peptides from protein sequences for downstream immunopeptidomics-style analysis.

stations.label: proteinfamilies
stations.blurb: Clusters protein sequences into families and builds family models. One of two pipelines in this chain that can hand its successors a ready-made samplesheet - it publishes one for proteinfold and one for proteinannotator, both pointing at the family representative sequences.

io.out: Protein family clusters + optional proteinfold / proteinannotator samplesheets

requires: --input samplesheet: sample, fasta (amino acid FASTA)
fasta extension must be .fa / .fasta / .faa / .fas, optionally .gz - a .pep file is rejected
--skip_proteinfold_samplesheet false to publish proteinfold/samplesheet.csv - it defaults to true, so the emitter is off unless asked for
--skip_proteinannotator_samplesheet false to publish proteinannotator/samplesheet.csv - same default

stations.label: seqsubmit
stations.blurb: Submits reads, metagenomic assemblies, MAGs and bins to ENA, registering the study and brokering the upload through Webin-CLI.
requires: --mode mags|bins|metagenomic_assemblies|reads - each mode has its own samplesheet schema

mags/bins --input samplesheet: id, fasta, accession, assembly_software, binning_software, binning_parameters, metagenome, co-assembly, broad_environment, local_environment, environmental_medium (+ optional fastq_1/2, completeness, contamination, genome_coverage, stats_generation_software, RNA_presence, NCBI_lineage)
fasta must be gzipped: .fa.gz / .fasta.gz / .fna.gz - an uncompressed FASTA is rejected
accession - the ENA run or assembly accession the MAG was derived from; that source must already be in ENA
ENA_WEBIN and ENA_WEBIN_PASSWORD supplied as Nextflow secrets
CheckM2 and CAT_pack databases (--checkm2_db, --cat_db) when completeness/contamination or lineage are not given

stations.label: proteinfold
stations.blurb: Predicts protein structures from amino-acid sequences. Computationally expensive; a stretch node. Dropped from the SIG metro map on 2026-08-11 but kept in scope here, because proteinfamilies already emits its input samplesheet.
requires: --input samplesheet at 2.0.0: fasta, plus either sequence or id (anyOf) - so the id,fasta sheet proteinfamilies emits is accepted unmodified
fasta extension at 2.0.0: .fa / .fasta / .faa / .yaml / .yml / .json - .faa passes, .gz does not
at 1.1.1 the column must be named sequence and the pattern is .fa / .fasta only, so the emitted sheet does NOT transfer - pin 2.0.0
--split_fasta when the input is a multi-FASTA, which _reps.faa is - one file holding every family representative

stations.label: proteinannotator
stations.blurb: Runs statistics over input protein FASTA and assigns function to each sequence with tools such as InterProScan. Reached from proteinfamilies, which emits its input samplesheet. Not on the SIG metro map.
requires: --input samplesheet: id, fasta - exactly the columns proteinfamilies emits
fasta extension .fa / .fasta / .faa / .fas, optionally .gz

stations.label: viralmetagenome
stations.blurb: Recovers and analyses viral sequences from shotgun metagenomic reads.

stations.label: metatdenovo
stations.blurb: De novo assembly and annotation of metatranscriptomes from shotgun RNA reads. Reads from all samples are collected into a single co-assembly, so it emits one assembly and one ORF set regardless of sample count.
requires: --input samplesheet: sample, fastq_1 (fastq_2 for paired-end)
--assembler - megahit or spades, no default
--orf_caller - prodigal, prokka or transdecoder, no default, required unless --user_orfs_* is set

stations.label: differentialabundance
stations.blurb: Tests features for differential abundance between conditions and renders a report.
requires: observations samplesheet: sample, plus one or more condition/grouping columns
abundance matrix: features as rows, observation IDs as columns matching the samplesheet
contrasts file: id, variable, reference, target (blocking optional)
feature annotations (optional but recommended)

The converter renames only those two columns, so sample names are identical to the --target reads output and run 02 stays comparable with run 04.

The sample rename off collection_date applies here too, since fetchngs supplies the ERX accession.

edges.note: viral contig FASTA -> phageannotator input, alongside the reads that produced it
edges.caveat: phageannotator's samplesheet requires sample, group, fastq_1 AND fasta, so this is not a one-file handoff: the contigs come from viralmetagenome, the reads from upstream, and group is a label neither pipeline emits. Extension matters too - the per-assembler contigs are published gzipped (<id>_spades.fa.gz) and pass, but tools_combined/<id>.combined.fa is not gzipped and phageannotator's pattern demands .gz. phageannotator also has no tagged release, so there is no pinned contract to validate against.

edges.note: viral contig FASTA -> phyloplace queryseqfile
edges.caveat: phyloplace 2.1.0 requires sample, queryseqfile, refseqfile, refphylogeny and model on every row. Only queryseqfile comes from viralmetagenome; the reference alignment, tree and substitution model are external inputs no upstream pipeline in this chain emits, and they have to be chosen per query clade. The same gap applies to the mag -> phyloplace row, which is still recorded as OPEN.

edges.note: filtered FASTQ -> ampliseq samplesheet. ampliseq is excluded from --generate_pipeline_samplesheets, whose pattern admits only taxprofiler and mag, so this sheet must be built by hand.
edges.caveat: Status derived from schemas, not from an execution - detaxizer is not run for the LMO pilot.

edges.repoStatus: OPEN - native emitter exists, output not yet verified
edges.note: --generate_downstream_samplesheets emits a taxprofiler samplesheet natively. detaxizer is one of two pipelines in this chain that ship a downstream samplesheet generator - proteinfamilies 2.5.0 is the other, via per-target skip_*_samplesheet flags rather than a pipeline-name enum.
edges.caveat: Whether taxprofiler accepts the generated sheet unmodified is untested. Deferred with detaxizer to the first host-related dataset.

edges.repoStatus: OPEN - native emitter exists, output not yet verified

edges.caveat: Whether mag accepts the generated sheet unmodified is untested. Deferred with detaxizer to the first host-related dataset.

edges.note: Filtered FASTQ -> sample,fastq_1,fastq_2. metatdenovo is excluded from --generate_pipeline_samplesheets, whose pattern admits only taxprofiler and mag, so the native emitter does not reach it. Added to the validation table 2026-08-11, when detaxizer re-entered the pilot as run 04.
edges.caveat: Mate synchronisation was verified in detaxizer 1.3.0 source rather than assumed, because a co-assembler cannot detect desynchronised pairs: MERGE_IDS unions the per-mate and per-classifier hit lists into one id file per sample, and modules/local/filter.nf applies that same list to both mates. Status derived from schemas and source, not from an execution - run 04 is prepared but has not been run.

edges.note: Site annotation, not a repo claim. createtaxdb 3.1.0 takes id + taxid + fasta_dna/fasta_aa, so its input comes from a reference set rather than from the read stream.
edges.caveat: This used to disagree with the metro map, which drew createtaxdb being fed by detaxizer - filtered reads, not reference FASTA. Raised for SIG review on 2026-08-10 and resolved in the 2026-08-11 redraw: the detaxizer -> createtaxdb edge is gone and createtaxdb is now fed from the reference FASTA input, matching its documented contract.

edges.note: db output path referenced in taxprofiler params
edges.caveat: This supplies taxprofiler's --databases sheet, not its reads. No sequencing runs travel this edge.

edges.note: MAG FASTA -> magmap reference input
edges.caveat: magmap 1.1.0 needs --genomeinfo (accno, genome_fna) plus its own read samplesheet - two inputs, not one handoff.

edges.repoStatus: CONVERSION REQUIRED - metadata, not just columns
edges.note: MAG/bin FASTA -> seqsubmit --mode mags|bins (assets/schema_input_genome.json). mag's bins are gzipped FASTA, which the schema accepts, so the sequence files transfer unchanged.
edges.caveat: The hard part is not the file, it is the row around it. seqsubmit requires per-MAG submission metadata mag does not emit: the ENA run or assembly accession the MAG derives from, assembly_software and binning_software with versions, binning_parameters, and four ENVO/MIxS environment fields (metagenome, broad_environment, local_environment, environmental_medium). Completeness and contamination can come from mag's own BUSCO/CheckM output or be recomputed by seqsubmit via CheckM2. A converter can fill the software and accession columns from the run provenance; the environment terms are a human judgement per dataset. Also needs ENA_WEBIN credentials as Nextflow secrets, so this edge cannot be exercised by a dry run.

edges.note: MAG/contig FASTA -> funcscan input
contig FASTA -> phageannotator input
edges.caveat: phageannotator has no tagged release, so there is no pinned contract to validate against.

edges.note: contig FASTA -> phyloplace input
predicted proteins FASTA -> input. One validation-table row covers metapep and proteinfamilies together; drawn here as two edges sharing that status.
edges.caveat: mag does not itself emit protein FASTA, so an ORF-calling / protein-extraction step belongs between these two stations. Worth proposing as an addition to the map.

edges.note: predicted proteins FASTA -> input. One validation-table row covers metapep and proteinfamilies together; drawn here as two edges sharing that status.
edges.caveat: mag does not itself emit protein FASTA, so an ORF-calling / protein-extraction step belongs between these two stations. Worth proposing as an addition to the map.

edges.repoStatus: CONVERSION REQUIRED - one-row samplesheet, no reformatting; exercised 2026-08-11
edges.note: --orf_caller prodigal publishes prodigal/<assembly>.faa.gz, an extension proteinfamilies accepts. Only a one-row sample,fasta samplesheet is needed; the sequences themselves transfer unchanged. Executed: 198,252 predicted proteins handed over via scripts/converters/metatdenovo_to_proteinfamilies.py, sheet accepted by proteinfamilies 2.5.0.
edges.caveat: Not yet on the metro map; a candidate addition, since metatdenovo is the only pipeline here that emits protein FASTA directly. The mapped route via mag needs an ORF-calling step first. The ORF caller matters: transdecoder publishes *.transdecoder.pep.gz, and .pep is not among proteinfamilies' accepted extensions - adding it upstream would make that route work too.

edges.note: --skip_proteinfold_samplesheet false (default true) publishes proteinfold/samplesheet.csv - id,fasta, pointing at the family representatives <samplename>_reps.faa. Emitted by run 03 on 2026-08-11; no proteinfold run has read it yet.
edges.caveat: Native against proteinfold 2.0.0 only. 2.0.0 accepts fasta plus either sequence or id, and allows .faa; 1.1.1 requires a column named sequence and matches .fa/.fasta only, so the emitted sheet is rejected there. _reps.faa is also one multi-FASTA of every representative rather than one file per structure, so proteinfold's own documented invocation for this sheet adds --split_fasta.

edges.note: --skip_proteinannotator_samplesheet false (default true) publishes proteinannotator/samplesheet.csv - the same id,fasta sheet, built from the same channel as the proteinfold one. Emitted by run 03 on 2026-08-11; no proteinannotator run has read it yet.
edges.caveat: proteinannotator 1.1.0 takes id + .fa/.fasta/.faa/.fas (optionally .gz), so this sheet needs nothing done to it. It is the cheaper of the two emitted handoffs to exercise - proteinfold needs --split_fasta and GPU-scale resources, this does not.

datasets.label: LMO pilot (provisional)
datasets.summary: Linnaeus Microbial Observatory, Baltic Sea brackish water at 2 m. Three collection dates carrying all three omics layers, 12 runs, 34.5 GB.
datasets.notice: Working recommendation only - the SIG dataset decision is still open, and the LMO sample-count discrepancy in DATASETS.md is unresolved.
datasets.routingBasis: Illustrative: items are routed by library_strategy alone. That is a drawing rule, not evidence that a run is suitable for a given pipeline.

fetchngs.note: Run 2026-08-10 on SLURM with Singularity. All 12 runs downloaded and md5-verified: 555,738,002 reads, 79,977,308,002 bases, 34.5 GB. Emitted samplesheet.csv is 12 rows by 39 columns, with collection_date at column 35. Three environment workarounds were needed (Nextflow 26.04 strict config parser, whitespace in ena_metadata_fields, and a wget container with no /etc/resolv.conf) - all recorded in RUNS.md and AGENTS.md. Provenance link in RUNS.md.

detaxizer.note: Prepared as run 04 on 2026-08-11, not yet executed. Reverses part of the 2026-08-10 decision to skip it: that decision was about filtering LMO against Homo sapiens, which is still declined - no host, and dropping metatranscriptome reads on human k-mer hits ahead of a co-assembly risks taking conserved and low-complexity microbial reads with them. What changed is the contaminant. Run 04 filters phiX (NC_001422.1, 5,386 bp) via --classification_bbduk instead: a sequencing spike-in that is supposed to be absent, that assembles into contigs, and whose ORFs went into run 03's 198,252 proteins. No biological risk, and no 60 GB kraken2 database, because KRAKEN2PREPARATION never runs with kraken2 classification off. Quantifying human content is now tracked as a separate measurement rather than a filter.

differentialabundance.note: The pilot has one amplicon and one metagenome run per date across three dates, metatranscriptome replicates that are library-level, and no condition or contrast metadata. differentialabundance 2.0.0 requires a contrasts file that cannot be built from this.

viralmetagenome.note: Not run. Reachable now that fetchngs -> viralmetagenome is tracked: the three WGS runs would feed it through the same converter metatdenovo used. Not on this pilot's active route, so no dots are drawn into it.

seqsubmit.note: Not run yet, and downstream of mag, which the pilot has not run either. Submission is meaningful even though the LMO reads came from ENA: the MAGs are new derived data and get their own accessions, referencing the source run accessions run 01 already collected. Needs ENA_WEBIN credentials as Nextflow secrets before it can be exercised.

metatdenovo.note: Run 2026-08-11. The six RNA-Seq libraries were converted to a sample,fastq_1,fastq_2 sheet by scripts/converters/fetchngs_to_reads_samplesheet.py, which renames samples off collection_date rather than the ERX accession fetchngs supplies. Single megahit co-assembly with prodigal ORF calling, specifically so a proteinfamilies-compatible .faa.gz is produced; eggnog, kofamscan and eukulele skipped. Out is 198,252 predicted proteins in one FASTA, not a sample count.

proteinfamilies.note: Run 2026-08-11 on the 198,252 proteins from metatdenovo, producing 405 protein families. One input row, because metatdenovo co-assembles into a single protein FASTA. Out is a family count, not a sample count, and it is not comparable to the 198,252 input proteins until min_seq_length 30 and cluster_size_threshold 25 are accounted for. The run also set the only two non-default parameters in the pilot - skip_proteinfold_samplesheet and skip_proteinannotator_samplesheet, both false - so it published ready-made samplesheets for both successors.

proteinfold.note: Not run. Its input samplesheet already exists: run 03 emitted proteinfold/samplesheet.csv on 2026-08-11, one row pointing at the 405 families' representative sequences. Blocked on nothing but compute - though it needs --split_fasta, since _reps.faa is one multi-FASTA, and version 2.0.0 specifically, because 1.1.1 rejects both the id column and the .faa extension.

proteinannotator.note: Not run. Its input samplesheet already exists: run 03 emitted proteinannotator/samplesheet.csv on 2026-08-11, the same single row of family representatives. proteinannotator 1.1.0 accepts it unmodified, which makes it the cheapest remaining test of nf-core samplesheet standardisation available to this project.
